elements.requirement: Proceedings for an offence under the Bribery Act 2010 may not be instituted in England and Wales except by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office.
elements.quote: No proceedings for an offence under this Act may be instituted in England and Wales except by or with the consent of— (a) the Director of Public Prosecutions,or (b) the Director of the Serious Fraud Office

elements.requirement: Proceedings for an offence under the Bribery Act 2010 may not be instituted in Northern Ireland except by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office.
elements.quote: No proceedings for an offence under this Act may be instituted in Northern Ireland except by or with the consent of— (a) the Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland, or (b) the Director of the Serious Fraud Office

elements.requirement: Proceedings for an offence under the Bribery Act 2010 may not be instituted in England and Wales or Northern Ireland by a person acting under the direction, instruction, or on behalf of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office, or to whom such a function has been assigned by either Director, except with the consent of the Director concerned.
elements.quote: No proceedings for an offence under this Act may be instituted in England and Wales or Northern Ireland by a person— (a) who is acting— (i) under the direction or instruction of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office, or (ii) on behalf of such a Director, or (b) to whom such a function has been assigned by such a Director, except with the consent of the Director concerned to the institution of the proceedings

elements.requirement: The Director of Public Prosecutions and the Director of the Serious Fraud Office must personally exercise any function of giving consent under subsection (1), (2), or (3).
elements.quote: The Director of Public Prosecutions and the Director of the Serious Fraud Office must exercise personally any function under subsection (1), (2) or (3) of giving consent

elements.requirement: The requirement for personal exercise of consent by the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office only permits an exception where the Director concerned is unavailable and another person has been designated in writing by that Director acting personally as authorised to exercise the function during unavailability.
elements.quote: The only exception is if— (a) the Director concerned is unavailable, and (b) there is another person who is designated in writing by the Director acting personally as the person who is authorised to exercise any such function when the Director is unavailable

elements.requirement: A person designated in writing to act when the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office is unavailable may exercise the consent function but must do so personally.
elements.quote: In that case, the other person may exercise the function but must do so personally

elements.requirement: The personal exercise and written designation rules in subsections (4) to (6) apply instead of any other provisions that would otherwise have allowed the consent functions of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office to be exercised by another person.
elements.quote: Subsections (4) to (6) apply instead of any other provisions which would otherwise have enabled any function of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of the Serious Fraud Office under subsection (1), (2) or (3) of giving consent to be exercised by a person other than the Director concerned

elements.requirement: Proceedings for an offence under the Bribery Act 2010 may not be instituted in Northern Ireland under section 36 of the Justice (Northern Ireland) Act 2002 without the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland.
elements.quote: No proceedings for an offence under this Act may be instituted in Northern Ireland by virtue of section 36 of the Justice (Northern Ireland) Act 2002 (delegation of the functions of the Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland to persons other than the Deputy Director) except with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland to the institution of the proceedings

elements.requirement: The Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland must personally exercise any function of giving consent under subsection (2) or (8) unless the function is exercised personally by the Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland under section 30(4) or (7) of the Justice (Northern Ireland) Act 2002.
elements.quote: The Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland must exercise personally any function under subsection (2) or (8) of giving consent unless the function is exercised personally by the Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland by virtue of section 30(4) or (7) of the Act of 2002

elements.requirement: Subsection (9) applies instead of section 36 of the Justice (Northern Ireland) Act 2002 regarding the consent functions of the Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland and the Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland under or by virtue of subsections (2) and (8).
elements.quote: Subsection (9) applies instead of section 36 of the Act of 2002 in relation to the functions of the Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland and the Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland under, or (as the case may be) by virtue of, subsections (2) and (8) above of giving consent
